name: Bounding Box Raymarching
aliases: Bounding Box Raymarching — Back-face ray casting, Raycasting via Bounding Box Rendering, Two-pass ray casting, WebGL Two-Pass Volume Ray Casting with Back-Face Culling
WebGL Two-Pass Volume Ray Casting with Back-Face Culling
definition: A two-pass GPU-based volume rendering technique implemented with modern OpenGL and GLSL, using a unit cube geometry to march rays through a 3D volume texture.
summary: Bounding Box Raymarching is a GPU-accelerated volume rendering technique that uses a two-pass process to rasterize back faces for ray endpoints, avoiding empty space computation by performing integration entirely within a fragment shader.
